turns.content: Star 1 shows 0.1 Angstrom of rotational broadening in the 6300-Angstrom [O I] line. Using c=3.00e5 km/s and ignoring inclination, write the Doppler relation and estimate its equatorial rotation speed.
Star 2 has a 20-day rotation period and a radius of 1.5 solar radii. Assuming rigid rotation and R_sun=6.96e5 km, calculate its equatorial speed.
Star 3 has v sin i=3.1 km/s and a rotational-axis inclination of 30 degrees. Recover its equatorial speed.
Star 4 has an activity-confirmed 9-day rotational-modulation period and a radius of 1.4 solar radii. Convert the quantities and calculate its equatorial speed.
Compare the four nominal speeds and identify the fastest rotator.

What observational and modeling uncertainties attach to that ranking, including line-profile broadening, stellar radii, periods, inclination, differential rotation, spot latitude, and the interpretation of the activity signal?
Which of those uncertainties is most capable of changing the nominal ordering, and why?
Report the fastest star, the four speed estimates, and a calibrated qualification of the ranking.
